entities.summary: Ligier Richier was a French sculptor active in Saint-Mihiel in Northeastern France from approximately 1520 to 1567. He is known for his contributions to the development of Baroque sculpture in the region, particularly in the creation of elaborate tombstones and reliquaries. Richier's work was highly regarded during his lifetime, and he was commissioned by several prominent Catholic churches and nobles to create intricate sculptures and decorations. His most famous works include the Saint-Mihiel Cathedral tomb of Saint Mihiel and the reliquary of the Holy Cross in the Saint-Mihiel Abbey. Despite his significant contributions to the art world, Richier's work fell into relative obscurity following his death in 1567, only to be rediscovered and celebrated in the 20th century. Richier's legacy can be seen in the many Baroque churches and monuments that still stand in Saint-Mihiel and the surrounding region. The city's rich artistic heritage, including Richier's work, continues to attract tourists and art historians interested in the development of Baroque sculpture in Europe.
